296	> }, handler)
297	> ```
298	
299	Note that Ajv will try to [coerce](https://ajv.js.org/coercion.html) values to
300	the types specified in the schema `type` keywords, both to pass validation and
301	to use the correctly typed data afterwards.
302	
303	> ⚠ Important:
304	> Fastify uses a custom [AJV configuration][1] such as `coerceTypes: 'array'`.
305	> Evaluate its behavior and verify if it meets the project requirements.
306	
307	[1]: https://github.com/fastify/ajv-compiler?tab=readme-ov-file#ajv-configuration
308	
309	The Ajv default configuration in Fastify supports coercing array parameters in
310	`querystring`. Example:
311	
312	```js
313	const opts = {
314	  schema: {
315	    querystring: {
316	      type: 'object',
317	      properties: {
318	        ids: {
319	          type: 'array',
320	          default: []
321	        },
322	      },
323	    }
324	  }
325	}
326	
327	fastify.get('/', opts, (request, reply) => {
328	  reply.send({ params: request.query }) // echo the querystring
329	})
330	
331	fastify.listen({ port: 3000 }, (err) => {
332	  if (err) throw err
333	})
334	```
335	
336	```sh
337	curl -X GET "http://localhost:3000/?ids=1
338	
339	{"params":{"ids":["1"]}}
340	```
341	
342	A custom schema validator can be specified for each parameter type (body,
343	querystring, params, headers).
344	
345	For example, the following code disables type coercion only for the `body`
346	parameters, changing the Ajv default options:
347	
348	```js
349	const schemaCompilers = {
350	  body: new Ajv({
351	    removeAdditional: false,
352	    coerceTypes: false,
353	    allErrors: true
354	  }),
355	  params: new Ajv({
356	    removeAdditional: false,
357	    coerceTypes: true,
358	    allErrors: true
359	  }),
360	  querystring: new Ajv({
361	    removeAdditional: false,
362	    coerceTypes: true,
363	    allErrors: true
364	  }),
365	  headers: new Ajv({
366	    removeAdditional: false,
367	    coerceTypes: true,
368	    allErrors: true
369	  })
370	}
371	
372	server.setValidatorCompiler(req => {
373	    if (!req.httpPart) {
374	      throw new Error('Missing httpPart')
375	    }
376	    const compiler = schemaCompilers[req.httpPart]
377	    if (!compiler) {
378	      throw new Error(`Missing compiler for ${req.httpPart}`)
379	    }
380	    return compiler.compile(req.schema)
381	})
382	```
383	
384	When type coercion is enabled, using `anyOf` with nullable primitive types
385	can produce unexpected results. For example, a value of `0` or `false` may be
386	coerced to `null` because Ajv evaluates `anyOf` schemas in order and applies
387	type coercion during matching. This means the `{ "type": "null" }` branch can
388	match before the intended type:
